(also operating as Universal EHR Solutions / UniEHR) is a very small, privately held healthcare IT company founded in May 2005, with roots going back to 2002. The company is based in the Garden Grove / Great Neck area and appears to have only a handful of employees (LinkedIn lists 3 visible employees, with a stated range of 11-50). The company was co-founded by Aaron Wachspress (CTO) and led by Mitchell C. Shapiro (President/Chairman). The lead developer listed on CHPL, Binh Pham, is based in Garden Grove, CA.\n\nThe company's flagship product is **Physician's Solution** (also branded as Universal EHR), a browser-based EHR and practice management system targeting ambulatory/outpatient practices of all sizes. The product is marketed as \"Designed FOR Doctors BY Doctors\" and emphasizes ease of use, low cost, and rapid deployment (claims of going live within one week). The company has a very small market footprint — it does not appear on major review sites like Capterra or G2, and its customer base appears to be concentrated in Southern California, particularly among Vietnamese-American medical practices in the Garden Grove/Westminster area (DAO Medical Group, a 30+ physician group, appears to be a primary customer and may have a business relationship with the product's developers).\n\nThe company was recognized as the preferred EMR vendor of the Florida Chapter of the American College of Cardiology and was used by Telemedik in Puerto Rico, per a 2011 press release. There is no evidence of significant market growth since then.\n\n## Product: Universal EHR (Physician's Solution)\n\nCHPL IDs: 9333\n\n### What It Is\n\nUniversal EHR (formerly/also known as Physician's Solution) is a browser-based, fully integrated EHR and practice management system for ambulatory/outpatient medical practices. It is certified as a Complete EHR under ONC standards. The system is designed for use across multiple specialties and practice sizes, from solo practitioners to multi-specialty groups.\n\nThe CHPL certification is for version 2.0.0 (certified 2018-03-12) and is broadly certified across 35+ criteria including clinical data (a)(1)-(a)(14), transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(3), patient portal/VDT (e)(1), clinical quality measures (c)(1)-(c)(3), public health reporting (f)(1)-(f)(2), and FHIR APIs (g)(7)-(g)(10)). The SED intended user description is \"OUTPATIENT CLINIC.\"\n\n### Users & Market\n\nThe product targets outpatient/ambulatory practices. Based on the patient portal login page and web research, known customers include:\n\n- **DAO Medical Group, Inc.** (Garden Grove, CA) — a 30+ physician, 100+ employee internal medicine and multi-specialty group. This appears to be the largest and most prominent customer. Michael M. Dao, MD, the group's principal, appears on LinkedIn as associated with both DAO Medical Group and universalehr.com, suggesting a deeper business relationship.\n- **BAN DUC DOAN, M.D., F.A.C.O.G.** — an OB/GYN practitioner\n- **Reform24 Medical Group** — appears in the patient portal login\n- **Southern California Vein and Wound Care Center** — a specialty practice\n\nThe customer base appears very small and geographically concentrated in Southern California. A 2011 press release mentioned customers in Puerto Rico (Telemedik) and endorsement from the Florida ACC chapter, but there is no evidence of broader adoption. The product does not appear on any major third-party EHR review sites (Capterra, G2, KLAS, Software Advice), which is consistent with a very small user base.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor press releases, the website, and product descriptions, Universal EHR / Physician's Solution includes the following modules and capabilities:\n\n**Clinical / EHR:**\n- Patient information management — entering and storing patient health information electronically\n- Clinical documentation and charting\n- Customizable templates designed by specialists for specific fields (OB/GYN, cardiology, pediatrics, internal medicine, and \"more than a dozen\" other specialty types)\n- Prescription ordering (e-prescribing)\n- Lab orders and results review\n- Diagnostic device interfacing (e.g., EKG machines — printed graphs automatically filed in patient chart)\n- Image management (labs and images accessible remotely)\n- Message review\n\n**Practice Management:**\n- Appointment scheduling\n- Claims and billing processing — described as a \"turnkey solution\" that either includes billing or interfaces with existing practice management/billing systems bidirectionally via XML or HL7 formats\n- Charge capture\n- Collections\n- Reporting and performance analysis\n- Superbill generation (evidenced by a \"superbill2000comp.pdf\" document on their site linked to DAO Medical Group)\n\n**Patient Engagement:**\n- **Patient Direct** — patient-facing portal (the patient portal at universalehr.com/Login/ is visible and functional)\n- **Doctor Direct** — physician-patient communication system; allows doctors to send test results and comments directly to a secure patient vault; described as reducing non-essential phone calls\n- **Physician's Portal** — message and data sharing between providers\n\n**Interoperability & Integration:**\n- HL7 and XML bidirectional interfaces with practice management/billing systems\n- Hospital, laboratory, and radiology interfaces\n- Referring physician communication\n- Interoperability Engine / API access (references to EMR Direct API terms of use on the website)\n- FHIR API support (certified for g(7)-(g)(10))\n\n**Enterprise:**\n- **Hospital's Solution** — described as a \"three-in-one package\" for enterprise control (mentioned in press releases, likely a separate product line for larger facilities)\n\n**Deployment:**\n- Cloud/browser-based — accessible from any internet-connected device (laptop, tablet, PDA, smartphone)\n- No third-party applications required\n- Described as supporting rapid deployment\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the features described above and the certification criteria, the system stores and manages:\n\n- **Patient demographics** — names, dates of birth, SSN (last 4 digits used for patient lookup), phone numbers, zip codes, email addresses, patient photos (evidenced by photo display on login)\n- **Clinical records** — patient charts, clinical notes, treatment procedures\n- **Prescriptions and refills** — medication orders and history\n- **Lab results** — laboratory data, test results\n- **Diagnostic images** — EKG graphs, imaging results automatically filed in charts\n- **Messages** — provider-to-patient communications via Doctor Direct, provider-to-provider messages via Physician's Portal\n- **Scheduling data** — appointment records\n- **Billing/claims data** — charge capture, claims, superbills, collections (whether built-in or via bidirectional interface with external PM system is somewhat ambiguous — the product is described both as a \"turnkey solution\" and as something that \"interfaces with\" existing PM systems)\n- **Reports** — performance analysis, clinical quality measures (certified for CQMs)\n- **Public health reports** — immunization and syndromic surveillance data (certified for f(1) and f(2))\n- **Security questions and authentication data** — patient portal security questions, usernames/passwords\n\n**Gaps and uncertainties:**\n- The vendor website is sparse and provides limited detail. Most specific feature information comes from press releases from 2011, which may not fully reflect the current state of version 2.0.0 (certified 2018).\n- Whether billing is fully integrated or primarily relies on bidirectional interfaces with external PM systems is unclear — both descriptions exist in vendor materials.\n- The \"Hospital's Solution\" product is mentioned in press releases but there is no current web presence for it; it's unclear if it's still offered.\n- No third-party reviews were found on any major review platform, making it impossible to corroborate vendor claims with user experiences (other than one unverifiable Capterra reference that may have been for a different product).\n- The product appears to have very limited documentation publicly available. Introduction \r\nThis guide is written for third party developers, including patients, who are developing software applications for accessing Protected Health Information (PHI) based on this public API documentation which allows applications to query health data secured by a Data Holder. Data Holders wishing to publish such a public-facing API should have their Health IT vendor register as a developer integrator of EMR Direct Interoperability Engine services at https://www.emrdirect.com/subscribe-developer . \r\nALWAYS KEEP IN MIND THAT ONLINE DATA TRANSFER IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR PERSON-TO-PERSON COMMUNICATION OF URGENT OR CRITICAL MEDICAL INFORMATION. \r\nThis documentation contains general information and important security information. General information will be marked as:\r\n Note: \r\n and important security information will be marked as: \r\n Important: \r\n \r\n 2. General Concepts \r\n a. Application Access Requests \r\n The API is a read-only RESTful HL7 FHIR® R4 API and follows the syntax described at https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/http.html . \r\nAll RESTful data access requests will be in the following format, in which the [base] URL will need to be obtained from the Data Holder, either directly or via directory information:\r\n GET [base]/[resource-specific parameters]… \r\n FHIR Bulk Data Access Group export is also supported as described in the Bulk Data Access IG. \r\n b.\tConnecting to the server \r\nThe server is accessed by clients through an https connection.\r\n Important: Local customer security policies must be in place to prevent unauthorized monitoring or eavesdropping of connections to the server. \r\n Important: Only TLS 1.2 connections are accepted. All plaintext connections will be refused. \r\n Note: Please limit your connection frequency to a value appropriate for your use case. Connection attempts which are more frequent than permitted by the bandwidth allocation for the data resource are not allowed. \r\n c. Authentication – Obtaining an Access Token \r\nPrior to making API requests, the client application must obtain an Access Token from the associated Authorization Server. The client software must support either the OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant or client credentials grant flow as detailed in RFC 6749 . For authorization code flow, a client ID and client secret are required. If the client application does not have a client ID and client secret for this purpose, the client application may obtain a client ID and client secret using the dynamic client registration protocol by submitting the required client information to the registration endpoint as detailed in RFC 7591 , by accessing the registration endpoint URL with a browser and completing the online form, by completing the manual registration process at the EMR Direct website, or by using UDAP Dynamic Client Registration . Please see section 3(j) below for the list Client app attributes required for registration. For client credentials flow, a client ID and registered public key are required. Public keys for client credentials grant access may be registered using UDAP Dynamic Client Registration or by contacting the Data Holder directly.\r\n \r\nFor client applications using authorization code grants, end user authentication is performed using a username and authentication credentials provided by the Data Holder. A healthcare organization may reuse existing patient portal credentials for this purpose, in which case the authenticated username maps to a unique patient portal user on the resource holder’s side. The end user should obtain these credentials directly from the Data Holder healthcare organizations from which they wish to access data.\r\n \r\n Note: Usernames and authentication credentials are established and reset by the Data Holder.\r\n \r\n When an end user is directed to the authorization endpoint, the user will be presented with a login screen where they can enter their credentials for the healthcare organization they are accessing. If the correct credentials are supplied and the end user grants access to the client application, an authorization code will be returned to the client that the client application can use to obtain an access token through the token endpoint as described in RFC 6749. For client credentials flow, the application obtains an access token directly from the token endpoint without user interaction.\r\n \r\nEach healthcare organization has a unique base URL that is used to access its Authorization Server. The required endpoint URLs are of the following form: \r\n \r\n \r\n Endpoint URL \r\n \r\n Authorization \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/authz \r\n \r\n Token \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/token \r\n \r\n Registration \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/register \r\n \r\n Manage \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/manage \r\n \r\n Revoke \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/revoke \r\n \r\n \r\n \r\n The complete OAuth 2.0 endpoint URLs for a given FHIR endpoint are published in that Data Holder's well known SMART configuration endpoint, as per Section 8.2 of the HL7 SMART App Launch specification .\r\n\r\n \r\n Refresh tokens: Client apps that use the authorization code flow and can securely store refresh tokens may request a refresh token by including the offline_access scope in the initial authorization endpoint request. Note that the end user may remove this scope during the authorization process. If a refresh token is permitted, it will be returned together with the access token as per RFC 6749 , and can be exchanged for a new access token as per RFC 6749 . Refresh token lifetime defaults to 90 days (but may be longer or shorter depending on the Data Holder's institutional policies). Each refresh token may be used once; a replacement refresh token will be issued when the client app uses a valid refresh token to obtain a new access token. Note that refresh tokens are not issued to Client apps that support client credentials code flow as these clients can authenticate directly to the token endpoint to obtain a new access token.\r\n \r\n PKCE support: Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) as defined by RFC 7636 is supported for Client apps that use the authorization code flow. The use of PKCE by such clients is optional. If used, Client apps must use only the S256 code challenge method. Please refer to RFC 7636 for details on how to use PKCE in requests to the authorization and token endpoints.\r\n \r\nAll requests to the API must include the access token transmitted in the Authorization header of the HTTP request as a bearer token as illustrated in RFC 6750 . If the access token is missing, expired, or otherwise not valid for the requested operation, the API will return a 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden response.\r\n \r\n 3. API Details \r\n a. Query a Specific Data Category Resource \r\n Client software must be capable of making HTTPS RESTful requests in accordance with the FHIR specification and consuming the FHIR Resources required by the United States Core Data for Interoperability ( USCDI ) or the FHIR Bulk Data Access specification. \r\n \r\n Resources returned conform to the resource profiles for HL7 FHIR R4 defined in the HL7 FHIR US Core Implementation Guide Release 3.1.1 found at https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/STU3.1.1 . All of the US Core Resource Profiles are supported except the optional US Core Medication Profile, as this API uses inline medication codes to represent medications instead of References to separate Medication resources.\r\n \r\n General specifications for FHIR resources and the associated data elements can be found at https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/resourcelist.html for other resource types without a US Core profile.\r\n \r\n Additional information for each required FHIR Resource or Data Element used to represent each data category can be found at the page above. For example, the Patient.name element is found at:\r\n https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/patient-definitions.html#Patient.name . The US Core FHIR IG profiles found at https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/STU3.1.1/profiles.html provide additional information on the meanings of elements and codes used by these profiles.\r\n \r\n Choices of data types: The US Core resource profiles permit a number of data types for certain resource elements as indicated by the [x] notation in the corresponding element names. The following table lists the data types supported for elements where a choice of data types is allowed by the US Core FHIR IG. However, please note that a particular Data Holder may not return all supported data types for a given element.\r\n \r\n Resource Data Element Supported choices \r\n AllergyIntolerance.onset[x] dateTime, Age, Period, Range, string \r\n CarePlan.scheduled[x] Timing, Period, string \r\n CarePlan.product[x] CodeableConcept, Reference \r\n Condition.onset[x] dateTime, Age, Period, Range, string \r\n Condition.abatement[x] dateTime, Age, Period, Range, string \r\n DiagnosticReport.effective[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Goal.start[x] date, CodeableConcept \r\n Goal.detail[x] Quantity, Range, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Ratio \r\n Goal.due[x] date \r\n Immunization.occurrence[x] dateTime, string \r\n Immunization.doseNumber[x] positiveInt, string \r\n Immunization.seriesDoses[x] positiveInt, string \r\n MedicationRequest.reported[x] boolean, Reference \r\n MedicationRequest.medication[x] CodeableConcept \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.asNeeded[x] boolean, CodeableConcept \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.doseAndRate.dose[x] Range, SimpleQuantity \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.doseAndRate.rate[x] Ratio, Range, SimpleQuantity \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.substitution.allowed[x] boolean, CodeableConcept \r\n Observation.effective[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Observation.value[x] Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, Ratio, SampleData, time, dateTime, Period \r\n Observation.component.value[x] Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, Ratio, SampleData, time, dateTime, Period \r\n Patient.deceased[x] boolean, dateTime \r\n Patient.multipleBirth[x] boolean, integer \r\n Procedure.performed[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Provenance.ocurred[x] dateTime, Period \r\n \r\n Choices of Reference resource types: The US Core resource profiles and the inherited FHIR R4 Observation Vital Signs profile permit a number of resource types to be referenced for certain \"Must Support\" resource elements where a value of type Reference is allowed for the corresponding element. The following table lists the resource types supported for such elements where a choice of referenced resource types is allowed. However, please note that a particular Data Holder may not return all supported resource types for a given element.\r\n \r\n \r\n Resource Data Element Supported choices \r\n CareTeam.participant.member US Core Patient, US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization \r\n DiagnosticReport.performer US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization \r\n DocumentReference.author US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization, US Core Patient \r\n MedicationRequest.reportedReference US Core Patient, US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization \r\n MedicationRequest.requester US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization, US Core Patient \r\n Observation.hasMember FHIR R4 Observation Vital Signs \r\n Provenance.agent.who US Core Practitioner, US Core Patient, US Core Organization \r\n \r\n \r\n b. Patient Selection \r\n \r\nTo search for patients, the application should request a bundle of Patient resources matching suitable search criteria. To facilitate this, client apps may include the following optional search parameters in a request for a Patient resource:\r\n \r\n \r\n Resource Data Element\t Search Parameter \r\n Patient.identifier\t identifier \r\n Patient.name\t name \r\n Patient.gender\t gender \r\n Patient.birthDate\t birthdate \r\n \r\n \r\n Please see the sections relating to search parameters in the US Core Patient Profile for details. Some Data Holders may support additional search parameters. Contact the Data Holder for more information on the supported search parameters or review the capability statement. \r\n \r\nFor example, to retrieve a bundle of Patient resources to which the app is authorized, where the patient's first or last name is Smith and the patient was born on July 4, 1976, the request could be formatted as: \r\n \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/Patient?name=Smith&amp;birthdate=1976-07-04 \r\n \r\n \r\nThe API will return a bundle of all patients (possibly zero) matching the search criteria. Only patients for which the app has been authorized access will be included in the results. Each patient returned in the search results is assigned a unique patient ID that can be found in the Patient.id element of the corresponding Patient resource. This patient ID can be included in subsequent requests to retrieve additional resources for that specific patient. \r\n \r\n c. Query for a Specific Data Category \r\n \r\nThe Patient resource can be retrieved by specifying a specific patient ID or by performing a search as discussed in section 3(b). The remaining resource types listed in Section 3(a) can be accessed for a specific patient as a Bundle of resources by performing a search by resource type or by patient compartment and specifying the patient ID in the request. For example, to retrieve a bundle of Immunization resources containing all available immunization history for Patient 1234, the request could be formatted as: \r\n \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/Immunization?patient=1234 \r\n \r\n \r\nThe following search terms can be used to isolate results for a single USCDI data class in cases where two or more data classes are represented by a single FHIR resource type:\r\n \r\n \r\n USCDI Data Class Search Parameter \r\n Health Concerns category=http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/CodeSystem/condition-category|health-concern \r\n Problems category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/condition-category|problem-list-item \r\n Smoking Status code=http://loinc.org|72166-2 \r\n Vital Signs category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category|vital-signs \r\n Laboratory Tests &amp; Laboratory Values/Results category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category|laboratory \r\n \r\n \r\nFor example, to retrieve the Smoking Status for Patient 1234, the request could be formatted as: \r\n \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/Patient/1234/Observation?code=http://loinc.org|72166-2 \r\n \r\n \r\nEach search request will return a bundle of zero or more results meeting the search criteria.\r\n \r\n d. Query for All Data as a CCDA document \r\n \r\n CCDA documents can be accessed within DocumentReference resources using the $docref operation as described in the US Core FHIR IG at: https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/STU3.1.1/OperationDefinition-docref.html . CCDAs are categorized as “Summary of Episode” Notes with LOINC code 34133-9. For example, to request a CCDA document covering all dates for patient 1234, the query could be formatted as: \r\n \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/DocumentReference/$docref?patient=1234 \r\n \r\n \r\nThe Base64 encoded CCDA XML data can be found in the DocumentReference.content.attachment.data element of the returned DocumentReference resource within the returned Bundle, if any.\r\n \r\n e. Query for a Subset of Data using Search Parameters \r\n \r\n The USCDI data classes or CCDA documents returned by the API may be filtered by supplying one or more optional search parameters, as detailed in the search parameter sections of the US Core Profiles for the corresponding resource type. The following table lists the supported search parameters for this purpose:\r\n \r\n \r\n Resource Data Element\t Search Parameter \r\n CarePlan.category\t category \r\n CareTeam.status\t status \r\n DiagnosticReport.code\t code \r\n DiagnosticReport.category\t category \r\n DiagnosticReport.effective\t date \r\n DocumentReference.type\t type \r\n DocumentReference.category\t category \r\n DocumentReference.date\t date \r\n Condition.category\t category \r\n MedicationStatement.status\t status \r\n MedicationRequest.intent\t intent \r\n Observation.code\t code \r\n Observation.category category \r\n Observation.effective\t date \r\n Patient.identifier\t identifier \r\n Patient.name\t name \r\n Patient.gender\t gender \r\n Patient.birthDate\t birthdate \r\n Condition.category\t category \r\n Procedure.performed\t date \r\n \r\n \r\nSome Data Holders may support additional search parameters. Contact the Data Holder for more information on the supported search parameters or review the capability statement.\r\n \r\n f. Error Handling \r\n \r\nIf the access token used in the request is invalid, expired, or the user has not been authorized to access the requested Resource, the API will return a 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden HTTP response.\r\n \r\nIf the request cannot be processed for other reasons (temporarily unavailable, unsupported resource type, system error, etc.), the API will return a 400 Bad Request HTTP response containing an OperationOutcome Resource with additional information regarding the issue contained in the OperationOutcome.issue element.\r\n \r\nHandling of OAuth-related errors is detailed in RFC 6749 .\r\n \r\nHandling of dynamic client registration errors is detailed in RFC 7591 .\r\n \r\n g. Supported clinical scopes \r\n \r\nApps identify the types of clinical data they would like to access by specifying one or more clinical OAuth scopes in their registration and authorization requests. Clinical scopes follow the format defined in the SMART App Launch Framework 1.0.0. Please see https://www.hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0/scopes-and-launch-context/index.html#scopes-for-requesting-clinical-data for additional details. Only read scopes are supported. Write scopes will be rejected. Applications may request patient-level, user-level, or system-level scopes for the following resource types:\r\n \r\n Resource \r\n AllergyIntolerance \r\n CarePlan \r\n CareTeam \r\n Condition \r\n Device \r\n DiagnosticReport \r\n DocumentReference \r\n Encounter \r\n Goal \r\n Group \r\n Immunization \r\n Location \r\n MedicationRequest \r\n Observation \r\n Organization \r\n Patient \r\n Practitioner \r\n PractitionerRole \r\n Procedure \r\n Provenance \r\n \r\n \r\n Some Data Holders may support additional resource types and clinical scopes. Contact the Data Holder for more information on the supported scopes or review the endpoint's capability statement to identify other resource types supported by that endpoint.\r\n \r\n Applications may also request \"wildcard\" scopes, e.g.: user/*.read \r\n \r\n h. OpenID Connect \r\n \r\nFor client apps that need to authenticate the end user using OpenID Connect, the server supports the required OpenID Connect functionality as specified in the SMART App Launch Framework version 1.0.0. Please refer to the following link for details: https://www.hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0/scopes-and-launch-context/index.html#scopes-for-requesting-identity-data \r\n \r\n i. Other Security Considerations \r\n \r\n Revoking access to patient data: End users can sign in to the management endpoint listed above to terminate access that the user has previously granted to a client application. Client applications may request revocation of tokens by making a request to the Data Holder's revocation endpoint as described in RFC 7009 .\r\n \r\n j. Attributes required for registration \r\n \r\nTo register a client for authorization code flow, the following information is required:\r\n \r\n \r\n Developer Name \r\n the name of the entity that created the app \r\n \r\n Developer Representative \r\n the name of the person completing this registration \r\n \r\n Client App Name \r\n the human-readable name of the app \r\n \r\n Redirect URI \r\n the app's redirection URI (https only) \r\n \r\n Client App URI (optional) \r\n a web page about the client app (http or https) \r\n \r\n Logo URI (optional) \r\n a URI to retrieve an image file with the app's logo (https only) \r\n \r\n Terms of Service URI (optional) \r\n a web page to view the app's terms of service (http or https) \r\n \r\n Privacy Policy URI (optional) \r\n a web page to view the app's privacy policy (http or https) \r\n \r\n Contact email \r\n an email address where the app developer may be contacted (use mailto: scheme) \r\n \r\n \r\nAdditionally, the client app developer will select the applicable characteristics of their application from the following:\r\n \r\n \r\n The client application is a confidential client capable of storing a client secret. \r\n The client application is a native application capable of securing a refresh token. \r\n \r\n \r\n Please see Section 2.1 of RFC 6749 for the definitions of 'confidential' and 'native application' as used above.\r\n \r\n 4. Frequently Asked Questions \r\n \r\n a. How do I access production API resources with my client application? \r\n \r\nPlease obtain FHIR endpoint information from a specific healthcare provider organization or trusted endpoint directory when you are ready to begin allowing client end users to access PHI with production credentials. Register your app using this documentation and the additional referenced specifications and website and test the app to ensure production readiness.\r\n \r\n b. How is business-to-business API access enabled? \r\n \r\nData Holders’ policies for professional access to their FHIR APIs vary. If your app requires privileged access to FHIR data outside of a Carequality, TEFCA, or other network agreement, you may request a UDAP certificate for trusted dynamic registration and JWT-based authentication when registering your app for client credentials flow, if supported by the Data Holder.\r\n \r\n c. How do end users and applications authenticate to the API? \r\n \r\nThe API is designed to support existing patient portal credentials via the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework as per RFC 6749 . The OAuth server also supports dynamic client registration as per RFC 7591 , UDAP Trusted Dynamic Client Registration, and clients that registered using the EMR Direct website, as discussed above in section 2(c).\r\n \r\n d. What data is available through the API? \r\n \r\nThe API will return all properly-formatted data provided by a connected data source system in response to a submitted query. Healthcare organizations may have their own policies and/or safety best practices that will dictate what data can be sent and when data is considered complete and/or ready to be sent. Please contact a healthcare organization directly for questions related to their specific policies.\r\n \r\n e. What additional options are offered? \r\n \r\n Interoperability Engine 2021 supports\r\n the SMART App Launch Framework (both standalone launch and EHR launch as per\r\n https://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0 ),\r\n SMART clinical scopes (patient, user, and system scopes),\r\n Open ID Connect ( https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html ), \r\n OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow, OAuth 2.0 refresh tokens, OAuth 2.0 revocation, \r\n the Unified Data Access Profiles ( UDAP&trade; ), FAST Security and Identity models, UMA (HEART profile),\r\nand more. Please contact the Data Holder directly\r\n to determine which additional options have been enabled by the Data Holder for a particular endpoint.\r\n \r\n \r\n Terms of Use: https://www.interopengine.com/open-api-terms ; inquire directly with integrators and Data Holders using Interoperability Engine for any additional terms and conditions that may apply.\r\n \r\nTrademark Notice: Interoperability Engine and the Interoperability Engine gears logo are trademarks of\r\nEMR Direct. Introduction \r\nThis guide is written for third party developers, including patients, who are developing software applications for accessing Protected Health Information (PHI) based on this public API documentation which allows applications to query health data secured by a Data Holder. Data Holders wishing to publish such a public-facing API should have their Health IT vendor register as a developer integrator of EMR Direct Interoperability Engine services at https://www.emrdirect.com/subscribe-developer . \r\nALWAYS KEEP IN MIND THAT ONLINE DATA TRANSFER IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR PERSON-TO-PERSON COMMUNICATION OF URGENT OR CRITICAL MEDICAL INFORMATION. \r\nThis documentation contains general information and important security information. General information will be marked as:\r\n Note: \r\n and important security information will be marked as: \r\n Important: \r\n \r\n 2. General Concepts \r\n a. Application Access Requests \r\n The API is a read-only RESTful HL7 FHIR® R4 API and follows the syntax described at https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/http.html . \r\nAll RESTful data access requests will be in the following format, in which the [base] URL will need to be obtained from the Data Holder, either directly or via directory information:\r\n GET [base]/[resource-specific parameters]… \r\n FHIR Bulk Data Access Group export is also supported as described in the Bulk Data Access IG. \r\n b.\tConnecting to the server \r\nThe server is accessed by clients through an https connection.\r\n Important: Local customer security policies must be in place to prevent unauthorized monitoring or eavesdropping of connections to the server. \r\n Important: Only TLS 1.2 connections are accepted. All plaintext connections will be refused. \r\n Note: Please limit your connection frequency to a value appropriate for your use case. Connection attempts which are more frequent than permitted by the bandwidth allocation for the data resource are not allowed. \r\n c. Authentication – Obtaining an Access Token \r\nPrior to making API requests, the client application must obtain an Access Token from the associated Authorization Server. The client software must support either the OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant or client credentials grant flow as detailed in RFC 6749 . For authorization code flow, a client ID and client secret are required. If the client application does not have a client ID and client secret for this purpose, the client application may obtain a client ID and client secret using the dynamic client registration protocol by submitting the required client information to the registration endpoint as detailed in RFC 7591 , by accessing the registration endpoint URL with a browser and completing the online form, by completing the manual registration process at the EMR Direct website, or by using UDAP Dynamic Client Registration . Please see section 3(j) below for the list Client app attributes required for registration. For client credentials flow, a client ID and registered public key are required. Public keys for client credentials grant access may be registered using UDAP Dynamic Client Registration or by contacting the Data Holder directly.\r\n \r\nFor client applications using authorization code grants, end user authentication is performed using a username and authentication credentials provided by the Data Holder. A healthcare organization may reuse existing patient portal credentials for this purpose, in which case the authenticated username maps to a unique patient portal user on the resource holder’s side. The end user should obtain these credentials directly from the Data Holder healthcare organizations from which they wish to access data.\r\n \r\n Note: Usernames and authentication credentials are established and reset by the Data Holder.\r\n \r\n When an end user is directed to the authorization endpoint, the user will be presented with a login screen where they can enter their credentials for the healthcare organization they are accessing. If the correct credentials are supplied and the end user grants access to the client application, an authorization code will be returned to the client that the client application can use to obtain an access token through the token endpoint as described in RFC 6749. For client credentials flow, the application obtains an access token directly from the token endpoint without user interaction.\r\n \r\nEach healthcare organization has a unique base URL that is used to access its Authorization Server. The required endpoint URLs are of the following form: \r\n \r\n \r\n Endpoint URL \r\n \r\n Authorization \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/authz \r\n \r\n Token \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/token \r\n \r\n Registration \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/register \r\n \r\n Manage \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/manage \r\n \r\n Revoke \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/revoke \r\n \r\n \r\n \r\n The complete OAuth 2.0 endpoint URLs for a given FHIR endpoint are published in that Data Holder's well known SMART configuration endpoint, as per Section 8.2 of the HL7 SMART App Launch specification .\r\n\r\n \r\n Refresh tokens: Client apps that use the authorization code flow and can securely store refresh tokens may request a refresh token by including the offline_access scope in the initial authorization endpoint request. Note that the end user may remove this scope during the authorization process. If a refresh token is permitted, it will be returned together with the access token as per RFC 6749 , and can be exchanged for a new access token as per RFC 6749 . Refresh token lifetime defaults to 90 days (but may be longer or shorter depending on the Data Holder's institutional policies). Each refresh token may be used once; a replacement refresh token will be issued when the client app uses a valid refresh token to obtain a new access token. Note that refresh tokens are not issued to Client apps that support client credentials code flow as these clients can authenticate directly to the token endpoint to obtain a new access token.\r\n \r\n PKCE support: Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) as defined by RFC 7636 is supported for Client apps that use the authorization code flow. The use of PKCE by such clients is optional. If used, Client apps must use only the S256 code challenge method. Please refer to RFC 7636 for details on how to use PKCE in requests to the authorization and token endpoints.\r\n \r\nAll requests to the API must include the access token transmitted in the Authorization header of the HTTP request as a bearer token as illustrated in RFC 6750 . If the access token is missing, expired, or otherwise not valid for the requested operation, the API will return a 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden response.\r\n \r\n 3. API Details \r\n a. Query a Specific Data Category Resource \r\n Client software must be capable of making HTTPS RESTful requests in accordance with the FHIR specification and consuming the FHIR Resources required by the United States Core Data for Interoperability ( USCDI ) or the FHIR Bulk Data Access specification. \r\n \r\n Resources returned conform to the resource profiles for HL7 FHIR R4 defined in the HL7 FHIR US Core Implementation Guide Release 3.1.1 found at https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/STU3.1.1 . All of the US Core Resource Profiles are supported except the optional US Core Medication Profile, as this API uses inline medication codes to represent medications instead of References to separate Medication resources.\r\n \r\n General specifications for FHIR resources and the associated data elements can be found at https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/resourcelist.html for other resource types without a US Core profile.\r\n \r\n Additional information for each required FHIR Resource or Data Element used to represent each data category can be found at the page above. For example, the Patient.name element is found at:\r\n https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/patient-definitions.html#Patient.name . The US Core FHIR IG profiles found at https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/STU3.1.1/profiles.html provide additional information on the meanings of elements and codes used by these profiles.\r\n \r\n Choices of data types: The US Core resource profiles permit a number of data types for certain resource elements as indicated by the [x] notation in the corresponding element names. The following table lists the data types supported for elements where a choice of data types is allowed by the US Core FHIR IG. However, please note that a particular Data Holder may not return all supported data types for a given element.\r\n \r\n Resource Data Element Supported choices \r\n AllergyIntolerance.onset[x] dateTime, Age, Period, Range, string \r\n CarePlan.scheduled[x] Timing, Period, string \r\n CarePlan.product[x] CodeableConcept, Reference \r\n Condition.onset[x] dateTime, Age, Period, Range, string \r\n Condition.abatement[x] dateTime, Age, Period, Range, string \r\n DiagnosticReport.effective[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Goal.start[x] date, CodeableConcept \r\n Goal.detail[x] Quantity, Range, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Ratio \r\n Goal.due[x] date \r\n Immunization.occurrence[x] dateTime, string \r\n Immunization.doseNumber[x] positiveInt, string \r\n Immunization.seriesDoses[x] positiveInt, string \r\n MedicationRequest.reported[x] boolean, Reference \r\n MedicationRequest.medication[x] CodeableConcept \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.asNeeded[x] boolean, CodeableConcept \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.doseAndRate.dose[x] Range, SimpleQuantity \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.doseAndRate.rate[x] Ratio, Range, SimpleQuantity \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.substitution.allowed[x] boolean, CodeableConcept \r\n Observation.effective[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Observation.value[x] Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, Ratio, SampleData, time, dateTime, Period \r\n Observation.component.value[x] Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, Ratio, SampleData, time, dateTime, Period \r\n Patient.deceased[x] boolean, dateTime \r\n Patient.multipleBirth[x] boolean, integer \r\n Procedure.performed[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Provenance.ocurred[x] dateTime, Period \r\n \r\n Choices of Reference resource types: The US Core resource profiles and the inherited FHIR R4 Observation Vital Signs profile permit a number of resource types to be referenced for certain \"Must Support\" resource elements where a value of type Reference is allowed for the corresponding element. The following table lists the resource types supported for such elements where a choice of referenced resource types is allowed. However, please note that a particular Data Holder may not return all supported resource types for a given element.\r\n \r\n \r\n Resource Data Element Supported choices \r\n CareTeam.participant.member US Core Patient, US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization \r\n DiagnosticReport.performer US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization \r\n DocumentReference.author US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization, US Core Patient \r\n MedicationRequest.reportedReference US Core Patient, US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization \r\n MedicationRequest.requester US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization, US Core Patient \r\n Observation.hasMember FHIR R4 Observation Vital Signs \r\n Provenance.agent.who US Core Practitioner, US Core Patient, US Core Organization \r\n \r\n \r\n b. Patient Selection \r\n \r\nTo search for patients, the application should request a bundle of Patient resources matching suitable search criteria. To facilitate this, client apps may include the following optional search parameters in a request for a Patient resource:\r\n \r\n \r\n Resource Data Element\t Search Parameter \r\n Patient.identifier\t identifier \r\n Patient.name\t name \r\n Patient.gender\t gender \r\n Patient.birthDate\t birthdate \r\n \r\n \r\n Please see the sections relating to search parameters in the US Core Patient Profile for details. Some Data Holders may support additional search parameters. Contact the Data Holder for more information on the supported search parameters or review the capability statement. \r\n \r\nFor example, to retrieve a bundle of Patient resources to which the app is authorized, where the patient's first or last name is Smith and the patient was born on July 4, 1976, the request could be formatted as: \r\n \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/Patient?name=Smith&amp;birthdate=1976-07-04 \r\n \r\n \r\nThe API will return a bundle of all patients (possibly zero) matching the search criteria. Only patients for which the app has been authorized access will be included in the results. Each patient returned in the search results is assigned a unique patient ID that can be found in the Patient.id element of the corresponding Patient resource. This patient ID can be included in subsequent requests to retrieve additional resources for that specific patient. \r\n \r\n c. Query for a Specific Data Category \r\n \r\nThe Patient resource can be retrieved by specifying a specific patient ID or by performing a search as discussed in section 3(b). The remaining resource types listed in Section 3(a) can be accessed for a specific patient as a Bundle of resources by performing a search by resource type or by patient compartment and specifying the patient ID in the request. For example, to retrieve a bundle of Immunization resources containing all available immunization history for Patient 1234, the request could be formatted as: \r\n \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/Immunization?patient=1234 \r\n \r\n \r\nThe following search terms can be used to isolate results for a single USCDI data class in cases where two or more data classes are represented by a single FHIR resource type:\r\n \r\n \r\n USCDI Data Class Search Parameter \r\n Health Concerns category=http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/CodeSystem/condition-category|health-concern \r\n Problems category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/condition-category|problem-list-item \r\n Smoking Status code=http://loinc.org|72166-2 \r\n Vital Signs category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category|vital-signs \r\n Laboratory Tests &amp; Laboratory Values/Results category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category|laboratory \r\n \r\n \r\nFor example, to retrieve the Smoking Status for Patient 1234, the request could be formatted as: \r\n \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/Patient/1234/Observation?code=http://loinc.org|72166-2 \r\n \r\n \r\nEach search request will return a bundle of zero or more results meeting the search criteria.\r\n \r\n d. Query for All Data as a CCDA document \r\n \r\n CCDA documents can be accessed within DocumentReference resources using the $docref operation as described in the US Core FHIR IG at: https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/STU3.1.1/OperationDefinition-docref.html . CCDAs are categorized as “Summary of Episode” Notes with LOINC code 34133-9. For example, to request a CCDA document covering all dates for patient 1234, the query could be formatted as: \r\n \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/DocumentReference/$docref?patient=1234 \r\n \r\n \r\nThe Base64 encoded CCDA XML data can be found in the DocumentReference.content.attachment.data element of the returned DocumentReference resource within the returned Bundle, if any.\r\n \r\n e. Query for a Subset of Data using Search Parameters \r\n \r\n The USCDI data classes or CCDA documents returned by the API may be filtered by supplying one or more optional search parameters, as detailed in the search parameter sections of the US Core Profiles for the corresponding resource type. The following table lists the supported search parameters for this purpose:\r\n \r\n \r\n Resource Data Element\t Search Parameter \r\n CarePlan.category\t category \r\n CareTeam.status\t status \r\n DiagnosticReport.code\t code \r\n DiagnosticReport.category\t category \r\n DiagnosticReport.effective\t date \r\n DocumentReference.type\t type \r\n DocumentReference.category\t category \r\n DocumentReference.date\t date \r\n Condition.category\t category \r\n MedicationStatement.status\t status \r\n MedicationRequest.intent\t intent \r\n Observation.code\t code \r\n Observation.category category \r\n Observation.effective\t date \r\n Patient.identifier\t identifier \r\n Patient.name\t name \r\n Patient.gender\t gender \r\n Patient.birthDate\t birthdate \r\n Condition.category\t category \r\n Procedure.performed\t date \r\n \r\n \r\nSome Data Holders may support additional search parameters. Contact the Data Holder for more information on the supported search parameters or review the capability statement.\r\n \r\n f. Error Handling \r\n \r\nIf the access token used in the request is invalid, expired, or the user has not been authorized to access the requested Resource, the API will return a 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden HTTP response.\r\n \r\nIf the request cannot be processed for other reasons (temporarily unavailable, unsupported resource type, system error, etc.), the API will return a 400 Bad Request HTTP response containing an OperationOutcome Resource with additional information regarding the issue contained in the OperationOutcome.issue element.\r\n \r\nHandling of OAuth-related errors is detailed in RFC 6749 .\r\n \r\nHandling of dynamic client registration errors is detailed in RFC 7591 .\r\n \r\n g. Supported clinical scopes \r\n \r\nApps identify the types of clinical data they would like to access by specifying one or more clinical OAuth scopes in their registration and authorization requests. Clinical scopes follow the format defined in the SMART App Launch Framework 1.0.0. Please see https://www.hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0/scopes-and-launch-context/index.html#scopes-for-requesting-clinical-data for additional details. Only read scopes are supported. Write scopes will be rejected. Applications may request patient-level, user-level, or system-level scopes for the following resource types:\r\n \r\n Resource \r\n AllergyIntolerance \r\n CarePlan \r\n CareTeam \r\n Condition \r\n Device \r\n DiagnosticReport \r\n DocumentReference \r\n Encounter \r\n Goal \r\n Group \r\n Immunization \r\n Location \r\n MedicationRequest \r\n Observation \r\n Organization \r\n Patient \r\n Practitioner \r\n PractitionerRole \r\n Procedure \r\n Provenance \r\n \r\n \r\n Some Data Holders may support additional resource types and clinical scopes. Contact the Data Holder for more information on the supported scopes or review the endpoint's capability statement to identify other resource types supported by that endpoint.\r\n \r\n Applications may also request \"wildcard\" scopes, e.g.: user/*.read \r\n \r\n h. OpenID Connect \r\n \r\nFor client apps that need to authenticate the end user using OpenID Connect, the server supports the required OpenID Connect functionality as specified in the SMART App Launch Framework version 1.0.0. Please refer to the following link for details: https://www.hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0/scopes-and-launch-context/index.html#scopes-for-requesting-identity-data \r\n \r\n i. Other Security Considerations \r\n \r\n Revoking access to patient data: End users can sign in to the management endpoint listed above to terminate access that the user has previously granted to a client application. Client applications may request revocation of tokens by making a request to the Data Holder's revocation endpoint as described in RFC 7009 .\r\n \r\n j. Attributes required for registration \r\n \r\nTo register a client for authorization code flow, the following information is required:\r\n \r\n \r\n Developer Name \r\n the name of the entity that created the app \r\n \r\n Developer Representative \r\n the name of the person completing this registration \r\n \r\n Client App Name \r\n the human-readable name of the app \r\n \r\n Redirect URI \r\n the app's redirection URI (https only) \r\n \r\n Client App URI (optional) \r\n a web page about the client app (http or https) \r\n \r\n Logo URI (optional) \r\n a URI to retrieve an image file with the app's logo (https only) \r\n \r\n Terms of Service URI (optional) \r\n a web page to view the app's terms of service (http or https) \r\n \r\n Privacy Policy URI (optional) \r\n a web page to view the app's privacy policy (http or https) \r\n \r\n Contact email \r\n an email address where the app developer may be contacted (use mailto: scheme) \r\n \r\n \r\nAdditionally, the client app developer will select the applicable characteristics of their application from the following:\r\n \r\n \r\n The client application is a confidential client capable of storing a client secret. \r\n The client application is a native application capable of securing a refresh token. \r\n \r\n \r\n Please see Section 2.1 of RFC 6749 for the definitions of 'confidential' and 'native application' as used above.\r\n \r\n 4. Frequently Asked Questions \r\n \r\n a. How do I access production API resources with my client application? \r\n \r\nPlease obtain FHIR endpoint information from a specific healthcare provider organization or trusted endpoint directory when you are ready to begin allowing client end users to access PHI with production credentials. Register your app using this documentation and the additional referenced specifications and website and test the app to ensure production readiness.\r\n \r\n b. How is business-to-business API access enabled? \r\n \r\nData Holders’ policies for professional access to their FHIR APIs vary. If your app requires privileged access to FHIR data outside of a Carequality, TEFCA, or other network agreement, you may request a UDAP certificate for trusted dynamic registration and JWT-based authentication when registering your app for client credentials flow, if supported by the Data Holder.\r\n \r\n c. How do end users and applications authenticate to the API? \r\n \r\nThe API is designed to support existing patient portal credentials via the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework as per RFC 6749 . The OAuth server also supports dynamic client registration as per RFC 7591 , UDAP Trusted Dynamic Client Registration, and clients that registered using the EMR Direct website, as discussed above in section 2(c).\r\n \r\n d. What data is available through the API? \r\n \r\nThe API will return all properly-formatted data provided by a connected data source system in response to a submitted query. Healthcare organizations may have their own policies and/or safety best practices that will dictate what data can be sent and when data is considered complete and/or ready to be sent. Please contact a healthcare organization directly for questions related to their specific policies.\r\n \r\n e. What additional options are offered? \r\n \r\n Interoperability Engine 2021 supports\r\n the SMART App Launch Framework (both standalone launch and EHR launch as per\r\n https://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0 ),\r\n SMART clinical scopes (patient, user, and system scopes),\r\n Open ID Connect ( https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html ), \r\n OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow, OAuth 2.0 refresh tokens, OAuth 2.0 revocation, \r\n the Unified Data Access Profiles ( UDAP&trade; ), FAST Security and Identity models, UMA (HEART profile),\r\nand more. Please contact the Data Holder directly\r\n to determine which additional options have been enabled by the Data Holder for a particular endpoint.\r\n \r\n \r\n Terms of Use: https://www.interopengine.com/open-api-terms ; inquire directly with integrators and Data Holders using Interoperability Engine for any additional terms and conditions that may apply.\r\n \r\nTrademark Notice: Interoperability Engine and the Interoperability Engine gears logo are trademarks of\r\nEMR Direct. However:\n\n- The Readme.txt in the export simply points to `https://build.fhir.org/nd-json.html` — a generic FHIR spec page, not custom documentation.\n- The EMR Direct Interoperability Engine documentation confirms US Core 3.1.1 profiles, but this is the (g)(10) API documentation, not (b)(10)-specific documentation.\n- The presence of `Invoice_1.ndjson` and `Appointment_1.ndjson` is interesting — these are not US Core resources. However, without a data dictionary or field mapping, there is no way to know what data is being omitted. There is no schema documentation to understand the Invoice or Appointment resources, and specialty-specific clinical data is unaccounted for.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is **very minimal** — a 6-page screenshot walkthrough of the export UI, with no technical detail about the exported data itself.\n\n- **No data dictionary**: There are no table definitions, field listings, or schema descriptions.\n- **No data type or value set documentation**: The only FHIR profile information comes from EMR Direct's generic (g)(10) API docs, which cover standard US Core resources.\n- **No worked examples or sample data**: The screenshots show a Notepad++ window with MedicationRequest NDJSON, but this is a redacted screenshot, not a downloadable sample file.\n- **No developer documentation**: A developer trying to import this data would need to reverse-engineer the NDJSON content with no vendor guidance on what to expect.\n- **Clearly a compliance checkbox**: The documentation was created in November 2023 as a quick Chrome \"Print to PDF\" of an internal page with screenshots. There is no field-level documentation whatsoever.\n- **Coded fields**: Not documented. The EMR Direct API docs reference US Core value sets generically.\n- **Relationships between entities**: Not documented. The FHIR references between resources (e.g., MedicationRequest.subject -> Patient) follow FHIR conventions, but there's no vendor-specific documentation.\n- **Versioning/change history**: None. Without field-level documentation of the Invoice resource content, it's impossible to assess whether billing coverage is meaningful or token.\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nUniversal EHR's EHI export documentation represents a **minimal compliance effort** from a very small vendor.
